description: There is deliberately no `schedule` here. Cadence is the runner cron's job (daily, 05:00 UTC) and having a second, independent gate is what broke this setup once already: #1 found that `before 9am on monday` against a `0 8 * * 1` cron left one hour of margin, and the one run that had happened started 3h29m late, so the window was missed and not a single PR was ever opened. GitHub Actions cron is best-effort, so any window narrow enough to be useful is also narrow enough to miss. With no `schedule`, whenever the runner actually manages to fire, Renovate is free to act, and a manual workflow_dispatch works at any hour instead of silently doing nothing.

Do not treat the drain workflow's branch updates as somebody having edited the branch. `drain-automerge-queue.yml` exists because the ruleset requires branches be up to date and `rebaseWhen: behind-base-branch` only rebases when Renovate next runs, so it advances the oldest automerge PR itself via `PUT /pulls/{n}/update-branch`. GitHub attributes the resulting merge commit to the App that made the call, `stateful-y-automation[bot]`, and Renovate reads an unrecognised last-commit author as a human edit: it posts an Edited/Blocked notice and stops managing the branch entirely. It then cannot rebase it, cannot regenerate it when the file set changes, and cannot supersede it with a newer version, so the branch is left depending on the drain workflow forever. This is how python-package-copier#329 got stuck as a half-bump that no config change could repair: the two automations were fighting and the drain workflow won by disabling the other. Every generated repo runs the same drain workflow under the same org App, so one address covers the fleet.

packageRules.description: Batch runtime, test and docs dependencies into one low-noise PR.
Lockstep the version-sensitive lint tools so local == CI stays true after an upgrade. prek pins the builtin hooks' implementations, so it moves with the linters.

Keep the template's action refs current, but on tags rather than digests. `pinDigests` here asked Renovate to write a SHA into a regex match that captures no `currentDigest` group -- there is nowhere to put it, so the write failed. That failure took the whole shared `renovate/pin-dependencies` branch with it, which is why python-package-copier alone stayed unpinned while the same run pinned all seven repos it generates: it is the only repo with a `template/` tree, so it is the only repo this rule touches. Digests belong downstream, where `helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests` writes them into the rendered workflows. Pinning here too would put a SHA on all 49 `uses:` lines of the template AND of every repo generated from it, turning each one into a conflict on every `copier update`.

Automerge action digest refreshes and action patch/minor bumps. The `automerge` label is not decoration: renovate-automerge.yml in each repo approves a bot PR only when it carries this label, because that workflow cannot key on the bot's account name (this App is `stateful-y-renovate[bot]`, not the hosted `renovate[bot]`). So the label must sit on exactly the rules that also set `automerge: true`, and nowhere else. Majors are excluded because an action major can change its inputs or outputs.

Same for the `# renovate:` annotated tool pins (uv, nox, git-cliff, gitleaks, cyclonedx-bom, twine), but ONLY in rendered workflows. Scoped positively to `.github/workflows/**` rather than by excluding `template/**`, because a later rule cannot take back an `addLabels` an earlier one applied: it would leave a PR labelled for automerge that Renovate will not merge, which the approve workflow would then approve and leave sitting. A bump inside template/ is seeded into all seven generated repos on their next update, so it keeps human review. NOTE this file scoping only holds because the template rule above sets `additionalBranchPrefix`, which splits template/** bumps into their own branch and therefore their own PR. Without that split, a dependency pinned in BOTH a rendered workflow and a template source lands in one PR whose file list matches this rule, and the whole PR gets labelled -- which is exactly what happened to the nox bump in python-package-copier#318 on the first live run. `astral-sh/uv` is excluded because the rule below deliberately un-splits it, which puts it back in exactly the both-trees-in-one-PR shape this scoping cannot label safely. The exclusion has to sit here rather than in a later rule, for the same reason the file scoping does: `addLabels` is additive and cannot be revoked.

Automerge patch/minor for the lint tools. These are dev-only, and a lint upgrade that breaks the build breaks it in CI, which blocks the merge by construction. Kept as its own rule rather than folded into the ones above so the lockstep grouping set earlier still applies. The grouped `python-dependencies` PR is deliberately NOT automerged: it batches runtime and dev dependencies into a single PR, so there is no safe half of it to merge unattended.

Do not fetch release notes for taiki-e/install-action. It publishes ~1200 releases whose bodies each enumerate every tool version they bump, an order of magnitude more history than anything else the fleet depends on. The template's `changelog.yml.jinja` carries the bare major `@v2`, which the template regex manager below reads as version 2.0.0, so the first bump off it spans the entire v2 line: rendering that PR body fetched the whole range and pushed Renovate's Node heap past 4GB. The process aborted (exit 134) at repository 3 of 13, so ten repos got no pass at all -- one dependency's changelog took down the whole fleet run. `prConcurrentLimit` had been hiding it, since the queue never reached this dependency until enough PRs ahead of it had automerged. The compare link in the PR body still shows what changed.

Keep uv's two halves in one PR. python-package-copier pins uv in its own workflows AND in the template sources it ships, and `test_repo_uv_pin_is_uniform_and_matches_the_version_shipped_to_projects` asserts the two are equal, so a split bump is red on both sides: the rendered half reads as the repo testing the template against a toolchain no generated project uses, and the template half reads as the mirror image. #329 and #330 deadlocked exactly that way, each blocking the other, while the same bump had merged as a single green PR the day before the split landed. Resetting `additionalBranchPrefix` to empty puts both trees back on one branch. This is the only dependency that needs it: a split is only fatal where a test ties the two pins together, and uv is the only pin under one.

customManagers.description: Bump versions annotated with a `# renovate:` comment (the pinned uv, nox, git-cliff, gitleaks, cyclonedx-bom and twine versions that no built-in manager reads). Covers rendered workflows AND the python-package-copier template sources that generate them: Renovate cannot see `.jinja` files, so the template's own seeds aged while every repo it generated moved ahead, and each fan-out then re-seeded a stale value into repos that had already passed it.

Keep the python-package-copier template's own `uses:` refs current, and pinned to digests. Renovate's github-actions manager reads `.github/workflows/*.yml`, so it maintains the workflows generated projects RUN but never the `.jinja` sources they are generated FROM: the template's refs moved only when a human edited a hand-written map, and every fan-out re-seeded whatever that human last wrote. Pinning here rather than only downstream keeps one notation on both sides -- with the template on tags and the fleet on digests, both moving, every action major bump would collide in seven repos at once.
